events.title: US jobs report (Employment Situation)
events.about: The BLS publishes last month's jobs added and the unemployment rate.
events.context: Now: US unemployment rate 4.10% for 2026-10 (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics).

watch: Jobs added last month and the revisions to earlier months
The unemployment rate
Average hourly earnings, a link between jobs and inflation

outcomes.outcome: Stronger than recent months
outcomes.meaning: More jobs or lower unemployment point to a firm economy. Fast wage growth can add to inflation pressure.

outcomes.outcome: Mixed
outcomes.meaning: Jobs and unemployment can point different ways, for example when more people start looking for work. The details explain which.

outcomes.outcome: Weaker than recent months
outcomes.meaning: Fewer jobs or rising unemployment point to a slowing economy, which central banks weigh when deciding rates.

scenarios.caution: Jobs figures are revised for two months after release, sometimes by a lot, so the first number is not the last word.

events.title: Bank of Canada rate decision
events.about: The Bank of Canada announces its target for the overnight rate at 9:45 am Eastern time.
events.context: Now: Bank of Canada policy rate 2.50% for 2026-11-17, last moved +0.25 pt on 2026-10-29 (Bank of Canada).

watch: The latest inflation figure next to the bank's target (2% for the Fed, ECB, Bank of Canada and Bank of England)
The latest jobs and unemployment figures
What the bank said at its last meeting about what would make it move

outcomes.outcome: It holds the rate
outcomes.meaning: Borrowing and savings rates linked to it stay where they are for now. The statement and press conference then matter most: they explain what the bank is watching.

outcomes.outcome: It raises the rate (usually by 0.25 points)
outcomes.meaning: Borrowing gets dearer across the economy, from variable-rate loans to new mortgages, and savings rates tend to rise. Banks raise rates to slow inflation.

outcomes.outcome: It cuts the rate (usually by 0.25 points)
outcomes.meaning: Borrowing gets cheaper and savings rates tend to fall. Banks cut to support growth and jobs when inflation is under control.

scenarios.caution: How people react often depends less on the decision than on how it compares with what was widely expected, and on the bank's words about what comes next.

events.title: Federal Reserve rate decision
events.about: The Federal Open Market Committee sets the target range for the federal funds rate; its statement comes out at 2 pm New York time on the last day.
events.context: Now: Effective federal funds rate 3.88% for 2026-11-17 (Federal Reserve Bank of New York).

events.title: US inflation report (Consumer Price Index)
events.about: The BLS publishes last month's consumer prices: the inflation rate over 12 months and its change from the month before.
events.context: Now: US inflation (CPI, over 12 months) 3.74% for 2026-09 (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics).

watch: Last month's 12-month inflation rate
Core inflation (without food and energy), which moves less from month to month
Which prices drove the change: housing, energy, food or services

outcomes.outcome: Inflation comes in higher than last month
outcomes.meaning: Prices are rising faster. It can make a central bank less likely to cut, or more likely to keep rates high for longer.

outcomes.outcome: About the same as last month
outcomes.meaning: Price pressure is steady. Attention moves to the details, such as core inflation and services prices.

outcomes.outcome: Inflation comes in lower than last month
outcomes.meaning: Prices are rising more slowly. It can give a central bank room to cut, if the slowdown lasts.

scenarios.caution: One month can be noisy: energy prices swing, and figures are sometimes revised. Several months together say more than one.

events.title: US producer prices (Producer Price Index)
events.about: The BLS publishes the prices businesses received last month, an early sign of price pressure.

watch: Last month's producer price change
Whether consumer prices (CPI) moved the same way

outcomes.outcome: Producer prices rise faster
outcomes.meaning: Businesses are charging more for their goods and services; some of it can reach shop prices later.

outcomes.outcome: Producer prices rise more slowly or fall
outcomes.meaning: Price pressure early in the supply chain is easing, which can show up in consumer prices later.

scenarios.caution: Producer prices are only one early signal; many costs never reach consumer prices one for one.
